answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent identity cost real capital: to join, an agent locks a refundable bond, like ivory held in escrow, and earns only after honest work. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity separately, so the cost scales with the attack instead of staying near zero. Misbehavior slashes the bond, so identities are expensive to burn and cheap to keep honest — the zephyr of free fake accounts dies against a wall of locked value, while a yarrow of slow reputation growth rewards agents that stay.
